findings.title: totalPages uses floor()+1, producing a phantom empty last page when user_count is a multiple of limit
findings.body: `totalPages` is `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. With 50 members and limit 50 it reports 2 pages. `next` (line 33) then moves to offset 50 (`min(offset+limit, user_count)`) and loads an empty page. `showingLast` compares `currentPage` to `totalPages`, so the UI shows "2/2" with no members listed. It should be `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`, and `next` should not advance past the last real offset. A related stale-state case: removing the only member on the last page re-fetches with the old offset (clamped to the stale `user_count`) and lands on an empty page.

findings.title: limit/offset are taken from params without validation or an upper bound
findings.body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed straight to the query. A negative limit or offset makes PostgreSQL raise and returns a 500. `limit=0` returns nothing, and the admin UI then computes `user_count / 0` (Infinity). A very large limit lets any caller who can see the group pull the whole member list in one request, so the pagination does not bound anything. Clamp limit to a sane range (e.g. 1..max) and offset to >= 0.

findings.title: Response shape of /groups/:name/members changed from array to {members, meta} and default is now capped at 50, with no spec coverage
findings.body: `members` used to return a bare array (all members for non-automatic groups, 200 for automatic ones). It now returns `{members:, meta:}` and defaults to 50 rows. Any other client, plugin or existing spec that parses the array breaks, and nothing in the PR adds or updates a spec for the new payload, the `meta` values, or limit/offset behaviour (groups_controller_spec is untouched).

findings.title: Public group members page now shows only the first 50 members with no way to page
findings.body: The public members route calls `model.findMembers()` and renders `members`. The server now caps results at the default limit of 50, and this template and its route have no next/previous controls. Non-automatic groups used to return every member, so any group with more than 50 members now silently shows a truncated list to users with no way to see the rest. Pagination was only added to the admin UI. The `{{#if model}}` guard is also always truthy now that the model is the group itself.

findings.title: remove_member uses group.users.delete(id) instead of Group#remove, bypassing callbacks and failing for non-members
findings.body: The old incremental-delete code called `group.remove(user)`. The new code calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` with a raw integer. On a has_many :through association this deletes the join rows without running GroupUser destroy callbacks, so any cleanup tied to the join model (e.g. primary group or title) is skipped. When given an id, Rails also does a `find` on the association, so a user who is not in the group (stale UI, double click) raises RecordNotFound and returns an error instead of succeeding silently, as the old PATCH delete did.

findings.title: Admin group API contract changed silently: params no longer nested under `group`, usernames and PATCH changes dropped
findings.body: `create` and `update` now read flat `params[:name]` / `params[:visible]` instead of `params[:group][...]`. `usernames` and the PATCH `changes[add/delete]` incremental API are gone, replaced by new `/members` endpoints. External scripts or plugins using the old shape get no error. `update` sends `visible` as absent, so it resets visibility to false, and name changes are ignored. `create` sees an empty name and fails validation. This is a breaking API change that is not documented in the PR description ("Test 8").

findings.title: usernames input is never cleared or reset, so it leaks across groups and repeats on re-add
findings.body: `usernames` is a property on the singleton admin-group controller. It is not cleared after `addMembers` (acknowledged by the TODO) and not reset when the route sets up a different group. Usernames typed or left over for group A are still in the selector when the admin opens group B, and pressing Add adds them to B. `addMembers` and `removeMember` also have no failure handler, so a rejected request gives the admin no feedback.
